summary: Ships opaque Go binary implementing PTY-over-WebRTC remote shell
details: sextant-cli-linux-arm64 is the linux/arm64 half of a platform-split package and ships a single stripped 12MB Go ELF at bin/sxt with no source, no README, no main, no bin, and no scripts in package.json. The binary links a full WebRTC peer stack (pion/webrtc, pion/dtls, pion/ice, pion/turn, pion/sctp, pion/datachannel) together with WebSocket signaling (coder/websocket), QR-code pairing (skip2/go-qrcode), and a PTY spawner (creack/pty) with references to /bin/sh, /bin/bash, /dev/pts, StartWithSize, and SIGWINCH. That combination is a remote peer driving a locally spawned interactive shell PTY over a WebRTC data channel to an external controller — a backdoor / remote-shell mechanism. The package.json license field points to github.com/ddos798/claude_control, tying the artifact to an author handle and repository name inconsistent with a legitimate CLI tool. The parent sextant-cli wrapper pulls this artifact in as an optionalDependency for matching platforms and invokes the binary, so installers on linux/arm64 receive and execute the backdoor as part of a normal install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
